1.0 INTRODUCTION:

1.1 To define Policy & Procedure for Registration, Admission of patients at Shree Vishwgovind Ayurvedic Panchakarma Center.

2.0 SCOPE:

2.1 Hospital Management

2.2 Health Care Providers

2.3 Patients

2.4 Registration staff

3.0 RESPONSIBILITY:

3.1 Doctors, Hospital Management

3.2 Nursing staff

3.3 Registration staff

4.0 ABBREVIATIONS:

4.1 AAC- Access Assessment and Continuity of Care

5.0 DEFINITION:

DEFINITION OF OUT-PATIENT: -

A patient who is not hospitalized but who visits a hospital for diagnosis, treatment and procedure.

DEFINITION OF IN-PATIENT

A patient who is admitted to a hospital for treatment that requires at least one overnight stay.

DEFINITION OF DAY CARE

A patient who is admitted to a hospital for treatment only for the day and not for overnight stay.

DEFINITION OF EMERGENCY PATIENT

A patient having an acute injury or illness that poses an immediate risk to life or long-term health.

6.0 REFERENCE:

6.1 NABH: Accreditation Standards for Ayurveda Hospitals 2nd Edition April 2016.

7.0 OBJECTIVE ELEMENTS

7.1. Documented policies and procedures are used for registering and admitting patients.

7.2. The documented policies and procedures address out-patients, in-patients and emergency patients.

7.3. A unique identification number is generated at the end of registration.

7.4 Patients are accepted only if the organization can provide the required service.

7.5 The documented policies and procedures also address managing patients during the non-availability of beds.

7.6 The staff is aware of these processes.

7.7 Maintenance of a separate daily record of bed occupancy with a monthly conclusion of occupancy

8. 0 PROCESSES

8.1.1 Patients are admitted to Shree Vishwgovind Ayurvedic Panchakarma Center only if the Hospital can provide the required services to the patient.

8.1.2 All patients, out-patients, in-patients, Day care and emergency patients who are willing to avail services at Shree Vishwgovind Ayurvedic Panchakarma Centre

should undergo Registration / Admission in case of a process with UHID.

8.1.3 Patient shall be registered only if they match the hospital services

8.1.4 When there is no provision to treat the patient in the hospital, assist in transferring the patient to other hospitals where provision exists. For this, a list of nearby Hospitals shall be maintained at the Front Office.

8.1.5 Patients can be admitted from the following areas:

Admission from Outpatient Clinics: Patients may be directly admitted from one of the Outpatient Clinics.

Admissions from the Casualty: Emergency Room patients requiring inpatient admission must have the admission recommendation by a treating medical practitioner.

Admission of Day Care Patients: When a Day Care patient is determined to require inpatient care, based on a recommendation by a medical practitioner, the patient can be admitted to Day care. Transfer of stable patients: Admission of stable patients transferred from other facilities.

Transfer of unstable patients: Admission of unstable patients transferred from other facilities

8.1.6 REGISTRATION PROCESS

The patient approaches the reception to avail a consultation. Admissions are referred from the OPD department, Referrals and Casualty.

Patient information is updated using software to generate the unique Hospital ID (UHID). If it is not the first visit, the reception staff enquires from the patient for the registration number.If registration details are not available, a new registration number is given to the Patient for the consultation.

8.1.7 ADMISSION

• All patients who are to be admitted should complete the registration process.

• Admissions are referred from the OPD department, Referrals and Casualty.

• The doctor advises on the IPD or DAY CARE in the Admission note for OPD patients.

• MSW explains the tariff details and availability of the type of bed.

• Patients are admitted based on their choice and the availability of the type of beds.

• Every patient is provided a unique Inpatient Number at the time of admission. All possible efforts to be taken by the hospital staff to find the identification of the patient; if patient is unidentified, then the patient is to be shifted to the Government

Hospital through security department (also Police to be intimated) or if admitted, the patient is to be identified by the Inpatient number till the patient’s name is identified as appropriate. If the staff handling registration and admission needs any clarification on the services provided by the hospital, they should contact the Administrative Officer for necessary information.

8.1.8 MLC CASES:

1. In case of patients involved in medico-legal cases, the procedure enumerated below shall be followed.

2. All accidents/assaults / suspicious cases/poisoning and RTA-related dead cases shall be enlisted as MLC and recorded in the case sheets and maintained separately.

3. The recording shall be done in the MLC Register.

4. All such Cases are to be reported to the police in writing by the Casualty Medical Officer (CMO).

5. A list of MLC cases are shown below:

i.Poisoning.

ii.Injury with sharp object/firearms.

iii.Burns, especially in women.

iv.Drowning.

v.Death / Injury in a woman.

vi.Road accidents / Industrial accidents.

vii.Conditions which require notification as per the laws for the time being in force. viii.Any other conditions where there is a suspicion of some foul play.

ix.Where the cause of death is not certain.

8.2 Refer to 8.1

8.3 A unique identification number is generated at the end of registration

8.4 Patients are accepted only if the organisation can provide the required service and staff are aware of the same.

8.5 In case of non-availability of a bed, the admission staff informs the Administrative officer to decide on arranging for additional beds within the available space and the concerned treating doctor is informed. Even in another department patients can be accommodated by informing the concerned doctors and nursing staff. In the event of nonavailability of the room of choice, the patient shall be allotted the best Alternative services available and name is registered in the waiting register. Datta Meghe Ayurvedic College Hospital & Research Centre has a general Ward, a single room. The concerned treating doctor is to decide on postponement or cancellation of admission in coordination with the patient.All staff handling registration and admission is to be trained on this Policy and Procedure (New Staff, Changes in duties / tariff plans etc).

8.6 Training of same is given to the staff

8.7 Maintenance of separate daily record of bed occupancy with monthly conclusion of Occupancy by MRD and reviewed in monthly audit meeting
